title: Trace debugging
point: Start from the symptom and walk back to the first span whose status or attributes are anomalous, because the loudest or costliest span is usually a consequence.
definition: Trace debugging is the method of finding a failure's root cause in a span tree. You start at the symptom, walk backwards through earlier spans, and stop at the first one whose status or attributes are wrong.

objective.text: Given a trace and a symptom, find the first anomalous span, explain why the most expensive or visible span is not the cause, and propose a fix.

misconceptions.claim: The most expensive span is where the bug is.
misconceptions.correction: Cost often piles up downstream of the real fault, such as a fallback model call after a timeout. Cost heat shows where money went, not why it went there.

misconceptions.claim: A span with status ok cannot be the cause.
misconceptions.correction: Status reports only what the span itself noticed. A guard that passes an injected instruction, or a retrieval that returns the wrong document, can be ok and still be the root cause.

l1: Write down the symptom first: a wrong answer, a slow run or a high bill. Then find the span that produced it, usually the final answer or the action the user saw.
Walk backwards in time and up the tree. At each earlier span, check its status and attributes against what a healthy run would show.
Stop at the first span that is anomalous. Everything after it is likely a consequence, however loud or expensive it looks.
l2: A customer is told refunds are allowed within 60 days, but the policy says 30. The llm.answer span is the largest in the trace and looks guilty.
Walking back, the retrieval.vector span one step earlier has status empty and zero hits. The answer model had no policy text and filled the gap from its own assumptions.
The fix is not a better answer prompt. It is routing an EMPTY retrieval to a clarifying question or a human, and fixing why retrieval found nothing.
l3: Cost heat is each span's share of total cost. It ranks spans by spend, which is the right view for a cost incident and the wrong one for a correctness incident.
Compare against a healthy trace for the same task. A guard that scanned 2,000 characters of a 6,400-character document looks normal until you see healthy runs scan whole documents.
Turn every diagnosed trace into a golden-set case and, where possible, a base-layer check. The debugging effort then keeps paying off on every later release.
